[The Start of Previous Conversation] user: What is Endianness? assistant: Endianness refers to how bytes of data are organized by the underlying computer architecture. There are two types of endianness: big-endian and little-endian. In big-endian format, the data is ordered starting with the most significant bit, while in little-endian format, it is ordered starting with the least significant bit. The Speech to Text service automatically detects the endianness of incoming audio. However, for audio in the l16 format, you have the option to specify the endianness, allowing you to disable auto-detection if necessary. [The End of Previous Conversation] [The Start of Current Turn Question] How can I specify the endianness? [The End of Current Turn Question] [The Start of Reference Answer] To specify the endianness when using the audio/l16 format, you can include the 'endianness' parameter in your format specification. This parameter should be set to either 'big-endian' or 'little-endian' based on the format of your audio data. For instance, if your audio data is in little-endian format and captured at 16 kHz, you would write the parameter as follows: audio/l16;rate=16000;endianness=little-endian. By default, the service automatically detects the endianness of incoming audio. However, explicitly specifying the endianness can be useful if auto-detection fails, especially for short audio files in the audio/l16 format. The Speech to Text service automatically detects the endianness of the incoming audio. Notes about audio formats * For the audio/l16 format, you can specify the endianness to disable auto-detection if needed. More information * For more information about endianness, see [Endianness](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness). Audio frequency endianness
Optional By default, the service auto-detects the endianness of incoming audio. But its auto-detection can sometimes fail and drop the connection for short audio in audio/l16 format. Specifying the endianness disables auto-detection. Specify either big-endian or little-endian. For example, specify the following parameter for audio data that is captured at 16 kHz in little-endian format:

audio/l16;rate=16000;endianness=little-endian

Section 5.1 of [Request for Comment (RFC) 2045](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045section-5.1) specifies big-endian format for audio/l16 data, but many people use little-endian format.
